reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch read Genesis 1:26's 'let us' as a plural of majesty expressing the one God's own fullness, not a council of separate deities.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Mark S. Smith catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Mark S. Smith, The Origins of Biblical Monotheism: Israel's Polytheistic Background and the Ugaritic Texts (2001).

sides.snippet: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness
sides.verseText: God said, \"Let us make man in our image, after our likeness: and let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, and over the birds of the sky, and over the cattle, and over all the earth, and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.\"
